subject: Cross-border access log extracts and retention — MedSys EU Q&A
messages:
From: Anna Kupfer <anna.kupfer@medsys-eu.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Tomáš Novák <t.novak@medsys-eu.com>
Date: 2028-03-12T08:15:00Z
Subject: Question: extracting access/audit logs for EU tenants

Hi Diego,

Quick one from our security team as we prepare for an upcoming audit: can Redwood produce an export of tenant access logs scoped to our EU region with the following details?

- Per-user authentication events (success/failure) with timestamps and source IP
- Admin console actions (who, when, action)
- Token creation/rotation events and associated keys
- Full event ordering for a given user/session for a selected timeframe (e.g., 2027-12-01 → 2028-02-28)

Two specific constraints: the exported artifacts must remain resident in the EU (no transit via US-based intermediate storage) and we need a deletion attestation showing records were removed from retention stores after the retention window.

Can you confirm capabilities, supported formats, and typical lead time for an extract like this? Also note we may need MD5/SHA checksums for the deliverables.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Kupfer
Security Lead, MedSys EU

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Anna Kupfer <anna.kupfer@medsys-eu.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-12T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: extracting access/audit logs for EU tenants

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can produce the extract you describe and keep the delivery and storage resident in the EU. Details below (high level) and I’ve looped in Jonas (infrastructure) and Evelyn (compliance) for specifics and attestation.

What we can provide now:
- Export contents: auth events, admin console audit, token lifecycle events, session ordering.
- Formats: compressed CSV, newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), or encrypted Parquet. We typically deliver a CSV/NDJSON pair for accessibility.
- Residency: export generation and final deliverable storage can be performed in an EU-only region (we use EU-west1/GCS or on-prem SFTP on request). We do not route the export via non-EU staging unless explicitly requested.
- Integrity: we can produce SHA256 checksums and sign the manifest.
- Lead time: for a single-tenant historical window up to 90 days, standard turnaround is 3–5 business days; for larger windows (~months) or multi-tenant slices, 7–10 business days depending on size and queue.

Open items for us to confirm:
1) Exact timeframe you want exported (start/end + timezone).
2) Which storage/delivery method you prefer (EU GCS link, SFTP to your appliance, or encrypted USB via courier).
3) Whether you require an internal deletion attestation (we can provide a signed report + retained export hashes) or a direct data-wipe certificate for your copies.

I’ll let Jonas and Evelyn fill in the technical delivery options and the attestation language.

— Diego
Diego Fernández
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Tomáš Novák <t.novak@medsys-eu.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Anna Kupfer <anna.kupfer@medsys-eu.com>
Date: 2028-03-12T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: extracting access/audit logs for EU tenants

Thanks, Diego — appreciate the quick confirmation. A few clarifications from our side:

- Timeframe: 2027-12-01T00:00:00Z through 2028-02-28T23:59:59Z.
- Delivery: prefer EU GCS with the bucket locked to our account; if not feasible, SFTP to our appliance (sftp.medsys-eu.local) is fine.
- Attestation: we need a deletion attestation from Redwood for the records removed from Redwood’s retention tier after the normal retention period (not just a hash manifest). The auditor expects an operator-signed statement including timestamps and the storage object names that were deleted.

Also: can you confirm whether exports include any derived telemetry that might contain tokenized PII, and whether Redwood performs any redaction by default?

— Tomáš

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, Anna Kupfer <anna.kupfer@medsys-eu.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-12T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: extracting access/audit logs for EU tenants

Hi all — Jonas from infra. Details and concrete options below.

1) Export generation and residency
- We can run the extract inside an EU-only VPC and write the output directly to an EU GCS bucket. Access controls: bucket ACLs will be restricted to MedSys service account + Redwood SRE principal (temp). We can set a signed URL for transfer or configure object lifecycle to auto-delete after your retrieval window.

2) Supported formats & size handling
- NDJSON: best for event-order reconstructability. Each event is a single JSON line with a session_id field so you can re-order reliably.
- Compressed CSV: columnar, easier for auditors; large exports will be sharded into parts (part-0000.csv.gz).
- Parquet (encrypted): best for large volume and queryability but requires a Parquet reader.

3) Checksums / manifest
- We will produce per-part SHA256 and a signed manifest file (manifest.json) with object names, sizes, and checksums. We can PGP-sign the manifest on request.

4) Deletion attestation / certificate
- Evelyn will provide the compliance wording, but the workflow is: we mark the export objects with a retention tag and delete them from production retention stores; after deletion, we generate a signed attestation PDF with
  - export object names
  - deletion timestamps (UTC)
  - operator signature (name, Redwood employee id)
  - reference to the internal deletion ticket (JIRA:SEC-4721)

5) PII / redaction
- By default we do not redact telemetry fields in audit exports. We can optionally apply field-level redaction prior to export (e.g., mask last octet of IPs, remove or pseudonymize email addresses). Redaction is configurable but may add to lead time and requires confirmation of which fields to transform.

Estimated schedule: if you confirm timeframe and GCS delivery by EOD tomorrow we can start a scoped export and target delivery by 2028-03-19.

Attachments: medsys_eu_log_scope_matrix.csv (suggested event list) and redwood-export-formats.pdf (formats & sample manifest).

— Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: Anna Kupfer <anna.kupfer@medsys-eu.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-13T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: extracting access/audit logs for EU tenants

Hi Anna / Tomáš — Evelyn from Compliance. Short note on the attestation language and retention interplay.

- Attestation scope: Redwood will provide a signed attestation that confirms deletion from Redwood-managed retention stores and lists the exact object names that were removed. Our attestation does not certify deletion of the copy once you pull the export into your environment; that is your responsibility unless you request Redwood to perform remote wipe of a customer-managed delivery endpoint (we offer a limited SFTP wipe flow for managed appliances).
- Retention windows: audit/access logs are retained by default for 12 months in production, with tiering that archives older records for up to 24 months depending on the account plan. If you need a custom retention window (shorter or legal-hold exempt), we can discuss contract amendments.
- Legal holds / eDiscovery: If MedSys requires legal hold, inform us immediately; we will suspend automated deletion and provide an eDiscovery export path with chain-of-custody metadata.

I’ll prepare the standard attestation template (PDF) and the required JIRA ticket to track the deletion run — referencing SEC-4721 as Jonas noted. Diego, please confirm delivery method and whether MedSys wants IP addresses redacted by default.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
